title: Module of Kähler differentials of a ring map
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. For an $A$-module $M$, an *$R$-derivation* $D:A\to M$ is an additive map with $D(fg)=f\,D(g)+g\,D(f)$ for $f,g\in A$ and $D(\varphi(r))=0$ for $r\in R$. The *module of Kähler differentials* of $A$ over $R$ is the pair $(\Omega_{A/R},\mathrm d)$ of an $A$-module $\Omega_{A/R}$ and an $R$-derivation $\mathrm d:A\to\Omega_{A/R}$ that is universal: for every $A$-module $M$, composition with $\mathrm d$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_A(\Omega_{A/R},M)\to\{R\text{-derivations }A\to M\}$. It exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism: $\Omega_{A/R}$ is the quotient of the free $A$-module on symbols $[a]$, $a\in A$, by the submodule generated by $[a+b]-[a]-[b]$, $[fg]-f[g]-g[f]$ and $[\varphi(r)]$, with $\mathrm da$ the class of $[a]$.
